verifier: zero-dependency Node.js strict CBOR/COSE, standalone-paper, series-DAG, rotation, observation, and closed-verdict verifier

cases.name: all eight paper releases are independently verifiable without any series bundle
cases.interpretation: Each standalone package binds exact content, ordered anonymous author keys, roles, contribution/AI declarations, and every listed endorsement.

cases.name: every release reference manifest and signed byte witnesses equal explicit WorkID tokens in exact content
cases.interpretation: The fixture recognizes only explicit urn:uuid WorkID tokens and their UTF-8 byte ranges; it does not claim to parse natural-language citation semantics.

cases.name: all eighteen endorsement objects are used exactly by their declared release
cases.interpretation: No author signature is silently reused as approval of a different release payload.

cases.name: a correctly signed release whose reference manifest disagrees with exact content is rejected
cases.interpretation: Author and release signatures alone do not make a reference declaration a text witness; the explicit WorkID token binding is also required.

cases.name: a correctly signed release whose citation-witness byte offset disagrees with exact content is rejected
cases.interpretation: A signed citation witness is checked against the content bytes fixed by the release hash; a shifted offset cannot be accepted as textual support.

cases.name: a correctly signed but noncanonical JSON release is rejected
cases.interpretation: The signed release body must have one profile-defined JSON byte representation, so duplicate fields, whitespace variants, and non-integer number spellings cannot create parser-dependent meanings.

cases.name: series epoch 0, authorized key rotation, epoch 1, and copy lineage signatures verify
cases.interpretation: Series bundles contain exact standalone release IDs; the epoch-1 key is accepted only through the old-key rotation statement.

cases.name: both local observation statements verify while explicitly disclaiming independent time
cases.interpretation: The fixture can order two local observations but does not upgrade them to RFC3161 or external-time evidence.

cases.name: mutual citations form a semantic cycle while cryptographic dependencies remain acyclic
cases.interpretation: Stable WorkIDs break the content-hash cycle; a later bundle maps both logical works to exact independently signed releases.

cases.name: P-v1 and Q-v1 mutually cite WorkIDs rather than each other's unresolved release hash
cases.interpretation: Both paper payloads can be finalized before the series bundle without a circular hash equation.

cases.name: canonical JSON corpus has the expected Node acceptance decisions
cases.interpretation: The corpus exercises key order, duplicate fields, whitespace, decimal and unsafe integers, UTF-8 values, and non-ASCII keys against the signed-object profile.

cases.name: artifact path resolver rejects parent-directory escapes
cases.interpretation: All profile-referenced paths must be relative descendants of the artifact project; a signed declaration cannot make the verifier read a parent path.

cases.name: Python and Node agree on every canonical JSON corpus decision
cases.interpretation: Independent runtimes must make the same accept/reject decision before a signed body is interpreted as a release, series, rotation, or observation object.

cases.name: independent Node verification agrees with the Python generation/reference path
cases.interpretation: Separate implementations agree on all signatures and on the semantic-cycle/cryptographic-DAG separation.

cases.name: pinned third-party archives match the audited source-provenance hashes
cases.interpretation: The offline build consumes only the two named, hash-pinned archives recorded in the source ledger.

cases.name: prior work is classified by source status instead of being presented as one undifferentiated novelty claim
cases.interpretation: The novelty boundary is the anonymous-scholarly-series profile and its executable counterexamples, not provenance, intrinsic identifiers, or signed statements themselves.

cases.name: scope boundaries remain explicit
cases.interpretation: The series layer adds lineage evidence but does not create independent time, natural-person identity, cross-paper identity links, originality truth, or legal non-repudiation.
